chat_history.content: give an estimate of the amount of the expression of the selected markers

Intensity data is not available at this dilation radius, so expression levels cannot be estimated from signal amplitude; coverage (segmented_voxels / total_voxels) is the only reliable metric here. Hoechst covers approximately 26% of total voxels (2,783,809,371 / 10,679,746,560), consistent with its expected role as a nuclear counterstain marking essentially all nuclei in the tissue — the dense, uniform blue signal filling the entire tissue volume in the image confirms broad, near-ubiquitous nuclear labeling. FOXP3 covers approximately 6.6% of total voxels (709,303,801 / 10,679,746,560), making it one of the lowest-coverage channels in this panel and consistent with FOXP3 being a transcription factor expressed only in a small subset of regulatory T cells (Tregs) — the scattered yellow puncta visible against the blue background in the image directly reflect this focal, sparse distribution. The roughly 4-fold difference in spatial coverage between Hoechst and FOXP3 underscores that FOXP3+ Tregs represent a minor cellular subpopulation within this tissue region, and FOXP3 is notably lower in coverage than other immune markers such as CD4 (~24.7%), CD3E (~20.7%), and CD8a (~19.0%), indicating Tregs are a restricted fraction of the total T cell infiltrate here.
